title: Authorization — what an organization permits, which is never what a person earned
description: A first-class object, deliberately NOT a kind of credential. Knowledge, skill and judgment are earned and are properties of a person; authority is granted, and is a relationship between a person, an organization and a scope of work. An approved signatory who leaves a laboratory keeps every competency they demonstrated and loses the signatory authority, because the laboratory granted it and the accreditation body recognized it AT THAT LABORATORY, FOR THAT SCOPE. A wallet that treated the two identically would let someone arrive at a new employer holding what looks like signing authority — a defect in the credential model, not in the taxonomy. This schema exists so that defect is structurally impossible rather than merely discouraged: `portable` and `walletExportable` are const false and cannot be authored otherwise.

subject.description: The person permitted to do the work. Same identifier as their competency credentials use, which is what allows an organization to check competence before granting — and what makes it tempting to treat the two objects alike. They are not alike.

grantedBy.description: The organization granting permission. Note there is no `issuer` here and no trust registry: an authorization is not verified by a stranger against a registry, it is asserted by an employer within its own boundary. That asymmetry is the point.

grantedByPerson.description: Who signed the grant. Usually a laboratory manager — the role registry records this as an authority the role commonly carries.

accreditationRecognition.description: Where an accreditation body recognizes this authority, the scope reference under which it does. Recognition is bounded by that scope and does not travel outside it.

scope.description:
What the person may actually do. An authorization with no scope is meaningless — "authorized" unqualified is the failure mode this object exists to prevent.

EVERY DIMENSION IS COMPUTABLE, and none of it used to be. `activities`, `methods`, `ranges` and `locations` were four arrays of free prose, so the scope-matching engine an accreditation body needs — *does this authorization cover this method, at this range, at this site* — could only be answered by a person reading the strings. "Signing certificates", "certificate signing" and "sign accredited certs" are three spellings of one activity and no comparison finds that.

A scope that participates in computation cannot exist only as prose. `deployment-scope.schema.json` is the model, and `measurement` shares its selector definitions rather than copying them.

activities.description:
What the grant permits, from a closed list. Adding a value is a deliberate schema change, which is the point: a free string let one activity be spelled three ways and matched none of them.

`sign-accredited-certificate` — signing under the laboratory's accreditation. `release-results` — issuing results to a customer. `approve-method` — admitting a method to the laboratory's scope. `conduct-assessment` — assessing somebody else's competence.

Four, because those are the four the profession names and this schema described in prose before it could check any of them. A grant that needs a fifth is a request to widen the enum, not a reason to reopen free text.

measurement.description:
Which measurement work the authority covers, resolved against the taxonomy exactly as a deployment scope is.

Required, and it is the dimension that carries the most weight: an authorization is a permission to do measurement work, so a grant that does not say WHICH is not bounded by anything a machine can check. `methods`, `ranges` and `locations` narrow it further and are optional — an absent dimension is unbounded, which is a real and common grant rather than an omission.

methods.description:
The methods the authority covers, IDENTIFIED rather than described. A scope of accreditation names methods — a published standard, or a laboratory procedure — and "does this authorization cover ISO 6789-2:2017" has to be answerable by comparison.

`revision` refines the match: stated here it must match exactly, because a revision can change what the method IS. Left off, the grant covers any revision — the reading most laboratory scopes intend, and its cost is that a revision materially changing the method does not automatically narrow the grant. That is a policy the organization has to manage, and it is at least now visible rather than buried in a string.

identifier.description: The method as the laboratory's scope names it — "ISO 6789-2:2017", "CP-014". Compared exactly.

source.description: The registered source, where the method is a published standard the corpus already knows about.

ranges.description:
Measurement ranges the authority covers. A signatory authorized for gauge blocks to 100 mm is not authorized at 500 mm, and this is where that is recorded.

STRUCTURED, BECAUSE THE COMPARISON IS ARITHMETIC. It was a list of strings, so "up to 100 mm" could be matched only by somebody reading it.

THE UNIT IS PART OF THE COMPARISON AND IS NEVER CONVERTED. A scope of 0–100 mm and a job at 0.5 m compare as 0.5 < 100 the moment units are ignored, which authorizes signing a certificate five times outside the granted range. This project does not ship a unit-conversion table to close that: a half-right conversion inside a metrology system is worse than none, and the failure would be silent. A unit mismatch makes the question UNDECIDABLE and says so — a real answer here, because "not covered" would wrongly block work and "covered" would wrongly permit signing.

quantity.description: What is measured — `torque`, `dc-voltage`, `length`. Compared exactly, so a laboratory has to spell it the same way twice; that is a lower price than a fuzzy match that quietly succeeds.

unit.description: The unit the bounds are expressed in. NEVER converted — see the note on this array. Write the SI unit symbol as the BIPM brochure gives it.

locations.description: Sites the authority covers. Identified rather than named in prose, for the same reason as everything else here: a grant valid at one site and not another is only enforceable if the two can be told apart by comparison.

expiresOn.description: Optional, because most authorizations end by event rather than by date — see `endsOn`. An authorization with neither is still bounded: it ends when the granting organization says it does.

basis.description: The competence this grant relied on, recorded as the elements and levels it was justified by. REQUIRED: an authorization granted on no competence basis is exactly the thing this system exists to make visible. Competence is a necessary input; it is never sufficient, because authorization also depends on appointment, current scope, organizational policy and continued employment.

credentialId.description: The credential relied on, where one exists. An organization may also grant on internally assessed competence that never became a credential; that is legitimate and should be visible as such.

portable.description: Cannot be authored otherwise. An authorization does not travel with the person under any circumstances, including when the person would very much like it to.

walletExportable.description: Belt and braces, deliberately. `portable` describes the object's nature; this constrains the one operation that would violate it. A wallet export that included authorizations would produce a holder who appears to arrive at a new employer already holding signing authority.

revocation.description: The properties that most sharply distinguish this from a credential.

unilateral.description: The granting organization may withdraw it without the holder's agreement and without notice.

appealableOnCompetence.description: A revoked authorization cannot be contested by demonstrating competence, because competence was never what conferred it. This is the field that stops the two objects collapsing into one another: a person may hold verified L4 judgment in CMM task-specific uncertainty and still not be authorized to release a CMM result, and both statements are true and non-contradictory.

endsOn.description: Events that end it automatically. Departure is the important one and is why nothing here is portable.
